motion.name: drill-in-enter

motion.purpose: Allows pointer travel between desktop triggers and panels before restoring Map.

motion.name: desktop-panel-exit
motion.purpose: Dismisses desktop dropdown overlays without rotating primary chevrons or moving layout.

motion.name: desktop-highlight-first-entry
motion.purpose: Places the shared dark highlight directly beneath the first hovered or focused Balloon, Briefing, or Regional target.

motion.name: desktop-highlight-move
motion.purpose: Glides one shared dark highlight between Balloon, Briefing, and Regional; direct-link movement closes dropdowns without breaking continuity.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: 0.01ms; drill-in animation none; desktop panel and highlight motion near-instant
motion.purpose: Effectively removes mobile transitions and makes desktop dropdown overlays and shared-highlight movement near-instant.

components.name: Search Field
components.description: Pill-shaped navigation search with cyan wayfinding and yellow caret emphasis.
components.html: <label class="ds-search"><svg aria-hidden="true" viewBox="0 0 24 24"><circle cx="11" cy="11" r="6"/><path d="m16 16 4 4"/></svg><input type="search" placeholder="search" aria-label="Search navigation"></label>
components.css: .ds-search { display:grid; width:100%; height:46px; grid-template-columns:44px minmax(0,1fr); align-items:center; border-radius:24px; background:var(--ink-raised,#0b4d73); } .ds-search:focus-within { outline:2px solid var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-search svg { width:22px; margin-left:15px; fill:none; stroke:var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); stroke-width:2; } .ds-search input { min-width:0; height:100%; padding:0 14px 0 2px; color:var(--text,#f4f8fb); background:transparent; border:0; outline:0; font:inherit; caret-color:var(--yellow,#ffdc72); } .ds-search input::placeholder { color:#8cc6e2; opacity:1; }

components.name: Profile Button
components.description: Compact circular account control using the system's attention signal.
components.css: .ds-profile { width:34px; height:34px; padding:0; color:#1d2a2f; font:800 1rem "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; background:var(--yellow,#ffdc72); border:0; border-radius:50%; cursor:pointer; } .ds-profile:hover { filter:brightness(1.04); } .ds-profile:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--focus,#ffdb4d); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Mobile Accordion Trigger
components.description: Mobile full-width navigation row with a rotating disclosure chevron; desktop primary chevrons remain static.
components.css: .ds-nav-trigger { position:relative; display:flex; width:100%; min-height:44px; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:12px; padding:8px 5px; color:var(--text,#f4f8fb); font:800 1rem/1.2 "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; letter-spacing:.02em; text-align:left; background:transparent; border:0; cursor:pointer; } .ds-nav-trigger::after { content:""; width:7px; height:7px; margin-right:3px; border-right:2px solid currentColor; border-bottom:2px solid currentColor; transform:rotate(45deg) translateY(-2px); transition:transform 150ms ease-out; } .ds-nav-trigger[aria-expanded="true"]::after { transform:rotate(225deg) translate(-1px,-1px); } .ds-nav-trigger:hover { color:var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); } .ds-nav-trigger:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--focus,#ffdb4d); outline-offset:2px; }

components.name: Drill-in Root Row
components.description: Full-width root category row that opens a dedicated history-backed child screen.
components.css: .ds-drill-row { display:flex; width:100%; min-height:52px; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:16px; padding:8px 5px; color:var(--text,#f4f8fb); font:800 1rem/1.2 "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; letter-spacing:.02em; text-align:left; background:transparent; border:0; border-bottom:1px solid transparent; cursor:pointer; } .ds-drill-row:hover { background:var(--wayfinding-wash,rgba(18,102,149,.24)); border-bottom-color:var(--line-soft,rgba(108,191,229,.28)); } .ds-drill-row:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--focus,#ffdb4d); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-drill-row svg { width:20px; flex:0 0 20px; fill:none; stroke:var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); stroke-width:2; }

components.name: Drill-in Screen Header
components.description: Sticky child-screen header with an explicit Back control and independently centered category title.
components.html: Map
components.css: .ds-screen-header { position:sticky; top:0; z-index:4; display:grid; grid-template-columns:92px minmax(0,1fr) 92px; min-height:56px; align-items:center; padding:0 8px; color:var(--text,#f4f8fb); background:var(--ink,#061f2d); border-bottom:1px solid var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); } .ds-screen-header h1 { grid-column:2; margin:0; font:800 1rem/1.2 "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; letter-spacing:.01em; text-align:center; } .ds-screen-back { display:inline-flex; min-height:44px; align-items:center; gap:3px; padding:0 6px 0 2px; color:var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); font:700 1rem/1.2 "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; background:transparent; border:0; cursor:pointer; } .ds-screen-back:hover { color:var(--text,#f4f8fb); } .ds-screen-back:focus-visible { outline:2px solid var(--focus,#ffdb4d); outline-offset:2px; } .ds-screen-back svg { width:22px; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:2; }

components.name: Destination Chip
components.description: Wrapping destination link for dense reports and map-layer inventories.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display:inline-flex; min-height:38px; align-items:center; gap:6px; padding:7px 8px; color:#dcecf3; font:400 .88rem/1.25 "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; text-decoration:none; background:var(--ink-raised,#0b4d73); border:0; border-radius:2px; cursor:pointer; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background:var(--ink-active,#126695); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible,.ds-nav-link[aria-current="page"] { color:#fff; outline:2px solid var(--yellow,#ffdc72); outline-offset:1px; } .ds-item-icon { display:inline-block; flex:0 0 20px; width:20px; height:20px; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#64e358,#1687dc); border-radius:2px; }

components.name: Latitude Longitude Toggle

components.css: .ds-switch-row { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px; color:var(--text-muted,#b8cfda); font:400 .9rem/1.2 "Trebuchet MS","Segoe UI",sans-serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-switch-row input { position:absolute; opacity:0; } .ds-switch-track { position:relative; width:40px; height:22px; background:#d9dde0; border-radius:13px; transition:background 150ms ease-out; } .ds-switch-track::after { content:""; position:absolute; top:-1px; left:-1px; width:24px; height:24px; background:#fff; border-radius:50%; box-shadow:0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.3); transition:transform 150ms ease-out; } .ds-switch-row input:checked + .ds-switch-track { background:var(--cyan,#6cc9f3); } .ds-switch-row input:checked + .ds-switch-track::after { transform:translateX(18px); } .ds-switch-row input:focus-visible + .ds-switch-track { outline:2px solid var(--focus,#ffdb4d); outline-offset:2px; }

narrative.overview:
The interface behaves like a compact operational index: information-rich, dark, and direct, with only the active hierarchy demanding attention. On mobile it supports disclosure-in-place and dedicated drill-in screens; on desktop it extends the same visual language into a persistent two-bar header and wide mega-navigation. Deep navy working surfaces keep the navigation visually continuous while brighter colors act as instruments—cyan points to controls and structure, lime marks categories, and yellow confirms focus, selection, and account identity.

Density is deliberate rather than cramped. Mobile participants begin on a minimal launcher that exposes only Accordion and Drilling, then enter the selected full-height journey. At 1024px and wider, the separate desktop surface begins with Map selected, keeps common map layers one step away in a secondary bar, and places the complete 26-layer inventory in a six-column mega panel. Decoration is subordinate to navigation state, legibility, and journey consistency.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy operational surfaces within near-black chrome.
A minimal two-choice participant launcher with no research controls.
Compact, wrapping destination chips and unmistakable accordion or drill-in state.
Cyan wayfinding, lime hierarchy labels, and scarce yellow emphasis.
Square-small content geometry balanced by pill and circular utility controls.
Restrained motion with a complete reduced-motion path.
Equivalent visible Back and browser Back behavior with restored keyboard focus.
A desktop-only primary bar, Map secondary bar, and six-column layer panel at 1024px and wider.
Intentional hover preview, click-to-pin persistence, and complete keyboard entry and return paths on desktop.

rules.name: The Three-Signal Rule
rules.body: Cyan means wayfinding and control, lime means hierarchy, and yellow means attention or selection; do not interchange their jobs casually.

rules.name: The Dark Continuity Rule
rules.body: Mobile menu bodies and the desktop Map layer panel remain uninterrupted navy working fields; structure comes from spacing, type, and selective rules rather than stacked decorative cards.

rules.name: The Weight-Before-Size Rule
rules.body: Inside the menu, create hierarchy through weight, color, and case before enlarging text; compact scanning is part of the product identity.

rules.name: The One-Level Rule
rules.body: Accordions expose only one top-level section at a time; drill-in navigation replaces the root list with one child screen. In both patterns, the visible inventory stays within one vertically scrolling region.

rules.name: The Same Exit Rule
rules.body: Visible Back and browser Back return to the same root state and restore focus to the category row that opened the child screen.

rules.name: The Participant Exit Rule
rules.body: Close and Escape leave either journey and return to the minimal launcher; they do not reveal an in-page test harness.

rules.name: The Launcher Boundary Rule
rules.body: The participant launcher exposes only Accordion and Drilling; the custom JavaScript accordion remains available solely through its direct internal query route.

rules.name: The Desktop Threshold Rule
rules.body: The primary bar, Map secondary bar, and mega panels exist only at 1024px and wider; they are a separate evaluation surface, not a responsive state of the 390px mobile prototype.

rules.name: The Desktop Reference Rule
rules.body: Desktop content follows its own supplied reference, including its wording, quick layers, and compact-panel composition; shared mobile content is not the authority for this surface.

rules.name: The Compact Panel Rule
rules.body: Briefing and Regional are full-width navy content panels with a cyan top border; never add an external grey caption or charcoal surround.

rules.name: The Flat Working Surface Rule
rules.body: Never use card shadows inside the menu; hierarchy there is tonal, typographic, and structural.

rules.name: The Shape-Semantics Rule
rules.body: Small square corners belong to dense destinations; pills and circles belong to singular controls.

rules.name: The Persistent Selected Page Rule
rules.body: Map remains cyan as the selected page while Briefing or Regional is previewed, open, or pinned; dropdown state supplements page state rather than replacing it.

rules.name: The Stationary Desktop Chrome Rule
rules.body: Keep primary chevrons pointing down and the Map sub-navigation in place behind dropdown overlays; communicate opening through the panel's clip-and-fade reveal, not rotating indicators or layout movement.

rules.name: The One Shared Highlight Rule
rules.body: Use one transform-driven dark layer for Balloon, Briefing, and Regional hover/focus continuity; first entry appears in place, later moves glide in about 260ms, and Map remains independently cyan.

rules.name: The Preview-Then-Pin Rule
rules.body: Hover and focus may preview desktop menus, but only activation pins a panel. Preserve the 110ms open and 260ms close intent windows so incidental pointer travel does not churn the navigation.

rules.name: The Escape Return Rule
rules.body: Escape always restores the default Map context and returns focus to the trigger responsible for the dismissed desktop panel.

dos: Do keep top-level accordion targets at least 44px tall and preserve one-open-at-a-time behavior.
Do use 52px drill-in root rows and keep the 56px Back/title header pinned above child-screen content.
Do let destination chips wrap naturally inside the vertical scrolling region.
Do use cyan, lime, and yellow according to the Three-Signal Rule.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, accurate expanded state, reduced-motion behavior, and semantic control structure.
Do make visible Back and browser Back restore the originating drill-in row's focus.
Do expose only Accordion and Drilling on the participant launcher.
Do center only the 390px by 844px frame on desktop and use the full viewport on mobile.
Do make Close and Escape return to the launcher from either journey.
Do keep the desktop mega-navigation at 1024px and wider, with Map selected and its secondary bar visible by default.
Do preserve all 26 supplied map layers in the six-column desktop panel and keep Briefing and Regional compact.
Do preserve desktop hover intent, click-to-pin behavior, Arrow/Enter/Space entry, and Escape focus return.
Do keep desktop chevrons static and reveal dropdown overlays in about 210ms, dismissing them in about 150ms.
Do use one continuous dark highlight across Balloon, Briefing, and Regional hover and focus states.
Do treat the desktop reference as the content authority for desktop labels, ordering, and panel composition.
donts: Don't add light cards, decorative gradients, or internal shadows that compete with the navigation inventory.
Don't use horizontal scrolling for destinations or map layers.
Don't turn every group into a bordered container; spacing and selective rules carry the structure.
Don't enlarge menu typography to manufacture hierarchy when weight, case, and color can do the job.
Don't animate state in a way that survives the user's reduced-motion preference.
Don't put explanatory copy or auxiliary controls around the participant frame.
Don't link the custom JavaScript accordion from the participant launcher.
Don't collapse the desktop navigation into the mobile frame or treat the two prototypes as one responsive document.
Don't open desktop menus on zero-delay pointer transit or dismiss a clicked-and-pinned panel on pointer leave.
Don't rotate Briefing or Regional chevrons or remove the Map sub-navigation to make room for their overlays.
Don't animate the first highlight entry from an unrelated origin or merge Map into the shared highlight.
Don't replace the desktop six-column layer panel with mobile wrapping chips or normalize desktop-specific copy to the mobile inventory.
